full_text_en:
Wu Shaohui v. Luxia Village Election Committee — Dispute over Voter Qualification Decision

Petitioner: Wu Shaohui, male, 32 years old, a villager of Luxia Village, Luxia Township, Pingnan County, Fujian Province, residing at No. 48 Xinxing West Road in the said village.

Petitioner Wu Shaohui, dissatisfied with the decision made by the Luxia Village Election Committee on his appeal for voter qualification, filed a lawsuit. The Pingnan County People's Court of Fujian Province, in accordance with the special procedure for voter qualification cases as stipulated in Chapter 15, Section 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, formed a collegial panel to hear this case, and notified the Luxia Village Election Committee to appear in court during the hearing.

Petitioner Wu Shaohui alleged: The petitioner's household registration is in Luxia Village, he is a villager of Luxia Village, and has always resided in the said village. The petitioner's right to vote has always been exercised in Luxia Village; in all previous elections of the villagers' committee, the petitioner has been a voter. In particular, during the villagers' committee election in 2000, the petitioner was even nominated by the villagers as an official candidate for the director of the villagers' committee. However, in this year's election, the village election committee ignored these objective facts and did not register the petitioner as a voter. After the petitioner filed an appeal, the election committee still made a decision on June 29, 2003 not to register the petitioner's voter qualification, which seriously infringed on the petitioner's right to vote and stand for election. The petitioner requests the people's court to set aside this decision according to law, order the village election committee to register the petitioner as a voter, and also request confirmation that the nomination of candidates for the villagers' committee of Luxia Village in this election is invalid.

The Pingnan County People's Court found through trial:

Although the petitioner Wu Shaohui resides at No. 48 Xinxing West Road in Luxia Village, his household registration has always been placed at the Luxia Township Central Primary School in Pingnan County. In all previous villagers' committee elections in Luxia Village, Wu Shaohui was registered as a voter. On June 12, 2003, Wu Shaohui moved his household registration from Luxia Township Central Primary School to Luxia Village, becoming a villager with non-agricultural household registration in the said village.

In 2003, due to the expiration of the term of office of the Luxia Village Villagers' Committee, an election was required by law. The election day was set as July 12, 2003, and voter registration began on June 7. The petitioner Wu Shaohui was not registered as a voter in the village. After Wu Shaohui appealed to the Luxia Village Election Committee, the committee held that although Wu Shaohui resided in the village, his household registration was transferred into the village after the voter registration date (June 7), and he was a villager with non-agricultural household registration in the village, with no contracted land in the village, and did not fulfill the obligations of a villager such as the "three retained funds and five unified contributions." According to the provision in the *Election Procedures for Villagers' Committees* issued by the Department of Civil Affairs of Fujian Province that "other persons with non-agricultural household registration whose household registration is managed in the village shall not be registered as voters," Wu Shaohui could not be registered in the village. In previous villagers' committee elections, although Wu Shaohui was registered as a voter in the village, these were all mistakes and should be corrected. Accordingly, on June 29, 2003, the committee made a decision: not to register Wu Shaohui's voter qualification. Wu Shaohui, dissatisfied with the decision, filed a lawsuit on June 30.

The Pingnan County People's Court held:

The right to vote and stand for election is a basic political right of citizens under the Constitution. Article 12 of the *Organic Law of the Villagers' Committees of the PRC*, revised and adopted at the Fifth Meeting of the Standing Committee of the Ninth National People's Congress on November 4, 1998, provides: "Villagers who have reached the age of 18, regardless of ethnicity, race, sex, occupation, family background, religious belief, education, property status, or length of residence, have the right to vote and stand for election; except for persons who have been deprived of political rights in accordance with law." The petitioner Wu Shaohui is now 33 years old, and according to law, he has voter qualification.

Article 14, paragraph 4 of the *Organic Law of the Villagers' Committees of the PRC* provides that the "specific election procedures for villagers' committees shall be prescribed by the standing committees of the people's congresses of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government." Article 11 of the *Election Measures of Fujian Province for Villagers' Committees*, revised at the 20th Meeting of the Standing Committee of the Ninth Fujian Provincial People's Congress on July 28, 2000, provides: "Any villager with voter qualification may register as a voter with the village election committee in the place where his or her household registration is located." The petitioner Wu Shaohui's household registration was moved to Luxia Village on June 12, 2003, and the election day of Luxia Village is July 12. According to the above provisions, before the election day, Wu Shaohui has the right to register as a voter with the election committee of Luxia Village, the place of his household registration.

Article 12 of the *Election Measures of Fujian Province for Villagers' Committees* provides: "The voter qualification once registered and confirmed shall be valid for a long term. Before each election, supplementary registration shall be made for voters who have become 18 years old after the last voter registration, who have newly moved into the village and have voter qualification, and who have had political rights restored after expiration of deprivation of political rights. Persons who have moved out of the village after voter registration, who have died, or who have been deprived of political rights in accordance with law shall be removed from the voter list." The petitioner Wu Shaohui, with voter qualification, although his previous household registration was not in Luxia Village, has always resided in Luxia Village; in all previous villagers' committee elections in Luxia Village, he was registered as a voter in that village; Wu Shaohui's voter qualification has been registered and confirmed by the Luxia Village Election Committee in previous terms and should be valid for a long term, and cannot be removed from the voter list except for special reasons such as moving out, death, or deprivation of political rights in accordance with law. Therefore, Wu Shaohui's request to register as a voter in Luxia Village has legal basis and should be supported. The provision in the *Election Procedures for Villagers' Committees* issued by the Department of Civil Affairs of Fujian Province that "other persons with non-agricultural household registration whose household registration is managed in the village shall not be registered as voters" conflicts with the provisions of the *Election Measures of Fujian Province for Villagers' Committees* and is invalid. The decision made by the Luxia Village Election Committee on June 29, 2003 based on that procedure is wrong and should be set aside.

Article 14, paragraph 1 of the *Organic Law of the Villagers' Committees of the PRC* provides: "The election of the villagers' committee shall be conducted by direct nomination of candidates by villagers who have the right to vote in the village." Article 15 of the *Election Measures of Fujian Province for Villagers' Committees* provides: "Candidates for members of the villagers' committee shall be directly nominated by villagers who have the right to vote, either individually or jointly. The number of candidates nominated by each voter shall not exceed the number of persons to be elected. No organization or individual may cancel, adjust, or change candidates directly nominated by voters in accordance with law or official candidates determined in accordance with law without going through legal procedures." The candidates for members of the Luxia Village Villagers' Committee were generated by direct nomination by villagers who have the right to vote. After the petitioner Wu Shaohui is registered as a voter in the village, he also has the right to nominate candidates. However, Wu Shaohui may not demand the cancellation, adjustment, or change of candidates nominated by other voters without legitimate reasons. Wu Shaohui's request to confirm that the nomination of candidates for the villagers' committee in this election is invalid lacks legal basis and is not supported.

In summary, the Pingnan County People's Court, in accordance with Articles 164 and 165 of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, rendered a judgment on July 8, 2003:

Set aside the decision made by the Luxia Village Election Committee of Luxia Township, Pingnan County not to register the petitioner Wu Shaohui's voter qualification.

After the judgment was pronounced, it immediately became legally effective in accordance with law.
